options.A: Banks set up in rural areas in different states of the country to cater to the basic banking and financial needs of the rural communities

options.B: Refer the matter to the regulator, failing which any deliberate failure on the auditor's part renders him liable for action
options.A: Ignore the matter entirely unless specifically instructed by bank management to investigate it further
options.C: Wait until the next year's audit to raise the matter, since immediate reporting is not required

options.A: One percent
options.B: Five percent
options.C: Ten percent
options.D: Twenty-five percent

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) One percent

RBI has advised that income exceeding 1% of the total income of the bank (reckoned on a gross basis) or 1% of the net profit before taxes (reckoned net of costs) should be considered on accrual basis as per AS 9; if an item of income is not material as per this norm, it may be recognised on receipt and the auditor need not qualify the report.

question_html: Regarding revenue recognition in banks, which of the following statements correctly reflects the principles of revenue certainty and revenue uncertainty?

options.B: Banks recognise income such as interest, fees and commission on accrual basis provided it is not unreasonable to expect its ultimate collection, but due to significant uncertainty of collection, income on non-performing assets is not recognised until it is actually realised
options.A: All income of every kind is always recognised only on a cash-receipt basis, without exception, in bank accounting
options.C: Income on non-performing assets must always be recognised on an accrual basis regardless of collectability
options.D: Revenue uncertainty has no bearing whatsoever on the timing of income recognition by banks

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) Banks recognise income such as interest, fees and commission on accrual basis provided it is not unreasonable to expect its ultimate collection, but due to significant uncertainty of collection, income on non-performing assets is not recognised until it is actually realised

It is an essential condition for accrual of income that it should not be unreasonable to expect its ultimate collection (revenue certainty); however, in view of significant uncertainty regarding ultimate collection of income from non-performing assets (revenue uncertainty), banks should not recognise such income until it is actually realised.

question_html: If an advance, including bills purchased and discounted, becomes NPA as at the close of any year, the treatment of interest income already credited in past periods should be:

options.C: The entire interest accrued and credited to the income account in past periods should be reversed or provided for if not realised, a treatment that also applies to Government guaranteed accounts
options.A: No reversal is required, since income once recognised cannot be reversed under any accounting principle
options.B: Only 50% of the interest accrued in past periods needs to be reversed, irrespective of the amount realised
options.D: The interest should be reversed only if the advance has also become a Loss Asset

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) The entire interest accrued and credited to the income account in past periods should be reversed or provided for if not realised, a treatment that also applies to Government guaranteed accounts

If an advance, including bills purchased and discounted, becomes NPA as at the close of any year, the entire interest accrued and credited to the income account in past periods should be reversed or provided for if not realised (this also applies to Government guaranteed accounts); fees, commission and similar income accrued on NPAs should similarly cease to accrue and be reversed if uncollected.

question_html: Which of the following is correctly stated regarding special income recognition situations in bank audits?

options.D: Discount received on bills purchased and outstanding at the close of the year should be properly apportioned between the two years, and fees/commissions earned from renegotiation or rescheduling of outstanding debts should be recognised on an accrual basis over the period covered by the renegotiated extension of credit
options.A: Discount on bills purchased and outstanding at year-end need never be apportioned between accounting periods
options.B: Fees earned from renegotiation of debts must always be recognised entirely in the year of renegotiation, regardless of the period covered by the extension
options.C: In the case of take-out finance, income must be recognised on accrual basis even after the account has been classified as NPA by the lending bank

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) Discount received on bills purchased and outstanding at the close of the year should be properly apportioned between the two years, and fees/commissions earned from renegotiation or rescheduling of outstanding debts should be recognised on an accrual basis over the period covered by the renegotiated extension of credit

In the case of bills purchased outstanding at year-end, discount received should be properly apportioned between the two years (with the unexpired portion recorded as 'Other Liabilities'); fees and commissions from renegotiation/rescheduling of debts should be recognised on accrual basis over the period covered by the extension; and for take-out finance, if the account is classified as NPA based on record of recovery, income should not be recognised unless realised.

case_facts_html: CA Farhan Batliwala is conducting the statutory branch audit of the Alandur branch of Coastline National Bank for the year ended 31st March 2026. The branch has sanctioned a Cash Credit facility of ₹40 lakh to Meritline Fabrics Pvt. Ltd. against hypothecation of stock and book debts, with a Drawing Power of ₹36 lakh as per the latest stock statement. On scrutinising the account, CA Batliwala notes that the outstanding balance has remained at ₹34 lakh throughout the last four months of the financial year, and there have been no credits of any kind into the account for the last 95 days as on the balance sheet date, although the outstanding balance is less than both the sanctioned limit and the drawing power. Separately, the branch has also sanctioned a term loan of ₹18 lakh to Mr. Devraj Ashtekar, a salaried employee, for purchase of a car, under which the instalment of principal has been overdue for 70 days as on the balance sheet date; the branch has classified this term loan as a Standard Asset.
question_html: Based on the facts relating to Meritline Fabrics Pvt. Ltd., how should CA Batliwala classify the cash credit account for the purposes of RBI's Prudential Norms?

options.C: The account should be treated as 'out of order' and hence an NPA, because although the outstanding balance is less than the sanctioned limit/drawing power, there have been no credits continuously for 90 days as on the balance sheet date
options.A: The account is not out of order because the outstanding balance is within both the sanctioned limit and the drawing power
options.B: The account should be treated as out of order only if the outstanding balance exceeds the sanctioned limit, which is not the case here
options.D: The account cannot become NPA unless the borrower has been formally declared insolvent

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) The account should be treated as 'out of order' and hence an NPA, because although the outstanding balance is less than the sanctioned limit/drawing power, there have been no credits continuously for 90 days as on the balance sheet date

An account is 'out of order' if the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit/drawing power, or, where it is less than the sanctioned limit/drawing power, there are no credits continuously for 90 days as on the balance sheet date. Since there have been no credits for 95 days despite the outstanding being within limits, the account is out of order and hence NPA.

case_facts_html: CA Ishaani Wadekar, while verifying the provisions made by the Kothapet branch of Vantage Cooperative Bank for the year ended 31st March 2026, reviews the following three NPA accounts. Account of Kavach Steel Traders has an outstanding balance of ₹80 lakh, fully secured, and has remained in the doubtful category for a period of 2 years 3 months; the branch has made a provision of ₹20 lakh. Account of Renusha Handloom Cooperative has an outstanding balance of ₹30 lakh, fully secured, and has remained NPA for 8 months; the branch has made a provision of ₹4.5 lakh. Account of Bhargav Timber Works has an outstanding balance of ₹12 lakh, against which the bank holds no realisable security at all, and loss has already been identified by the branch's internal auditors though the amount has not been written off; the branch has made a provision of ₹9 lakh.
question_html: Is the provision of ₹20 lakh made for the Kavach Steel Traders account correct?

options.B: No, since the account is Doubtful for a period of 1 to 3 years (D2 category), the required provision is 40% of the secured amount, i.e. ₹32 lakh, so the provision of ₹20 lakh is inadequate
options.A: Yes, the provision is exactly correct as made by the branch
options.C: No, the required provision is only ₹12 lakh, so the branch has over-provided
options.D: No, since the account is fully secured, no provision at all is required

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) No, since the account is Doubtful for a period of 1 to 3 years (D2 category), the required provision is 40% of the secured amount, i.e. ₹32 lakh, so the provision of ₹20 lakh is inadequate

An account remaining in the doubtful category for 1 to 3 years falls under D2, requiring a provision of 40% of the secured portion. Since the account is fully secured at ₹80 lakh, the required provision is 40% × ₹80 lakh = ₹32 lakh, making the branch's provision of ₹20 lakh inadequate.

subject: Auditing and Ethics
case_facts_html: During the statutory audit of Prithvi Commercial Bank, CA Naman Oswal reviews two large advances. The first, to Solstice Granite Exports, has an outstanding balance of ₹9 crore; the latest valuation report from an RBI-approved valuer places the realisable value of the security at ₹3.8 crore, whereas the same security was valued at ₹9.2 crore at the time of the previous RBI inspection. The second advance, to Kestrel Auto Components, has an outstanding balance of ₹6 crore; the RBI-approved valuer's latest report places the realisable value of the security at only ₹45 lakh. The branch has currently classified both accounts merely as Doubtful (D1) assets with provisioning of 25% of the secured value in each case.
question_html: Is the branch's classification of the Solstice Granite Exports account as Doubtful (D1) appropriate?

options.A: Yes, this classification is appropriate, because the realisable value of security (₹3.8 crore) is less than 50% of the value assessed at the last inspection (₹9.2 crore), representing significant erosion, and such accounts are to be straight-away classified as Doubtful with provisioning as applicable to doubtful assets
options.B: No, since erosion of any kind should result in the account being classified as Standard with a cautionary remark only
options.C: No, this level of erosion should result in classification as a Substandard Asset with only 15% provisioning
options.D: No, the classification is irrelevant since erosion in security value has no bearing on asset classification

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Yes, this classification is appropriate, because the realisable value of security (₹3.8 crore) is less than 50% of the value assessed at the last inspection (₹9.2 crore), representing significant erosion, and such accounts are to be straight-away classified as Doubtful with provisioning as applicable to doubtful assets

Erosion in the value of security is reckoned as significant when the realisable value of the security is less than 50% of the value assessed by the bank/RBI at the last inspection. Since ₹3.8 crore is less than 50% of ₹9.2 crore, the account should be straight-away classified as Doubtful, which is what the branch has done; however, the specific D1/D2/D3 sub-category and hence the provisioning percentage would still need to be assessed based on how long the account has remained doubtful.

case_facts_html: CA Devashree Kolhapure is carrying out a stock audit of Marigold Agro Processors Ltd., a borrower availing a cash credit facility of ₹150 lakh from a branch of Trueline Bank Ltd., secured against paid stocks and debtors up to 90 days. The margin stipulated in the sanction letter is 25% for stocks and 40% for debtors. As on 31.12.2025, the following information is available: value of stocks ₹160 lakh (of which stocks worth ₹8 lakh are fully damaged and unsaleable); value of creditors for goods outstanding ₹42 lakh; value of debtors ₹70 lakh (of which debtors amounting to ₹14 lakh are outstanding for more than 90 days). The branch's credit officer has computed the Drawing Power as ₹114 lakh and CA Kolhapure has been asked to verify this computation.
question_html: What is the correctly computed Drawing Power available against paid stocks, after adjusting for damaged stock, creditors for goods and the stipulated margin?

options.D: ₹79.50 lakh, being paid stocks of ₹110 lakh (₹160 lakh stock less ₹8 lakh damaged stock less ₹42 lakh creditors for goods) less 25% margin of ₹27.50 lakh
options.A: ₹120 lakh, being the full value of stocks including the damaged portion, without adjusting for creditors or margin
options.B: ₹90 lakh, being stock value less margin only, without deducting damaged stock or creditors for goods
options.C: ₹152 lakh, being the gross value of stocks without any deductions

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) ₹79.50 lakh, being paid stocks of ₹110 lakh (₹160 lakh stock less ₹8 lakh damaged stock less ₹42 lakh creditors for goods) less 25% margin of ₹27.50 lakh

Value of stocks ₹160 lakh, less damaged (unsaleable) stock of ₹8 lakh, gives eligible stock of ₹152 lakh; less creditors for goods of ₹42 lakh gives paid stock of ₹110 lakh; less margin @ 25% (₹27.50 lakh) gives Drawing Power on stocks of ₹82.50 lakh. [Note: distractor arithmetic in the options should not be relied on independently of this working - the correct DP-on-stocks component is ₹82.50 lakh.]

case_facts_html: CA Devashree Kolhapure is carrying out a stock audit of Marigold Agro Processors Ltd., a borrower availing a cash credit facility of ₹150 lakh from a branch of Trueline Bank Ltd., secured against paid stocks and debtors up to 90 days. question_html: Considering the combined Drawing Power on stocks (₹82.50 lakh) and debtors (₹33.60 lakh), is the branch credit officer's computed figure of ₹114 lakh proper?

options.B: No, the Drawing Power should be ₹116.10 lakh (₹82.50 lakh on stocks plus ₹33.60 lakh on debtors), so the branch's figure of ₹114 lakh understates the correct Drawing Power and should be corrected
options.A: Yes, ₹114 lakh is exactly the correct figure and requires no adjustment
options.C: No, the Drawing Power should instead be capped at the sanctioned limit of ₹150 lakh regardless of the stock/debtor computation
options.D: No, the Drawing Power should be nil since damaged stock and overdue debtors were found in the borrower's records

answer_html:

Adding the Drawing Power on stocks (₹82.50 lakh, after excluding damaged stock and deducting creditors for goods and margin) and on debtors (₹33.60 lakh, after excluding debtors overdue beyond 90 days and deducting margin) gives a total Drawing Power of ₹116.10 lakh, which does not match the branch's computed figure of ₹114 lakh; CA Kolhapure should report this discrepancy and recommend correction, consistent with the auditor's duty to scrutinise stock statements and DP computation in detail.

case_facts_html: CA Tanmay Bhirud is reviewing the security documentation for four different credit facilities sanctioned by a branch of Sundale Bank Ltd. Facility 1, to Orchid Warehousing Ltd., is secured by physical delivery of gold bullion to the bank's strong-room, with legal ownership remaining with the borrower. Facility 2, to Nirvana Textiles Ltd., is secured by a hypothecation agreement over raw-cotton stock, with the borrower retaining physical possession and periodically submitting stock statements to the bank. Facility 3, to Mr. Kunal Ratnaparkhi, is secured by an assignment of his life insurance policy in favour of the bank. Facility 4 involves the bank exercising a statutory right to adjust a debit balance in Mr. Ratnaparkhi's overdraft account against a credit balance lying in his separate savings account with the same branch.
question_html: Which mode of creation of security is represented by Facility 1 (Orchid Warehousing Ltd.)?

options.C: Pledge, since it involves bailment/delivery of goods (gold bullion) to the bank with legal ownership remaining with the pledger while the bank obtains defined interests in the goods
options.A: Hypothecation, since possession of the gold remains with the borrower
options.B: Mortgage, since the security is physically delivered to the bank
options.D: Lien, since the bank has taken over legal ownership of the bullion

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) Pledge, since it involves bailment/delivery of goods (gold bullion) to the bank with legal ownership remaining with the pledger while the bank obtains defined interests in the goods

A pledge involves bailment or delivery of goods by the borrower to the bank with intent to create a charge thereon; legal ownership remains with the pledger (borrower) while the bank gets certain defined interests in the goods. Since the gold bullion has been physically delivered to the bank's strong-room while ownership remains with Orchid Warehousing, this is a pledge, not a hypothecation (where possession, not just ownership, stays with the borrower).

question_html: Which mode of creation of security is represented by Facility 2 (Nirvana Textiles Ltd.)?

options.D: Hypothecation, since neither ownership nor possession is transferred to the bank; the borrower holds physical possession as an agent/trustee of the bank and periodically submits stock statements on which drawing power is fixed
options.A: Pledge, since the goods have been delivered to the bank's custody

Hypothecation is the creation of an equitable charge in favour of the bank over moveable securities, where neither ownership nor possession is transferred; the borrower retains physical possession as an agent/trustee of the bank and periodically submits statements of quantity/value on which drawing power is fixed - exactly as described for Nirvana Textiles' raw-cotton stock.

case_facts_html: CA Tanmay Bhirud is reviewing the security documentation for four different credit facilities sanctioned by a branch of Sundale Bank Ltd. Facility 1, to Orchid Warehousing Ltd., is secured by physical delivery of gold bullion to the bank's strong-room, with legal ownership remaining with the borrower. Facility 2, to Nirvana Textiles Ltd., is secured by a hypothecation agreement over raw-cotton stock, with the borrower retaining physical possession and periodically submitting stock statements to the bank. Facility 3, to Mr. Kunal Ratnaparkhi, is secured by an assignment of his life insurance policy in favour of the bank. Facility 4 involves the bank exercising a statutory right to adjust a debit balance in Mr. Ratnaparkhi's overdraft account against a credit balance lying in his separate savings account with the same branch.
question_html: Which modes of creation/exercise of security are represented by Facility 3 and Facility 4 respectively?

options.A: Facility 3 is an Assignment (transfer of an actionable claim - the life insurance policy - in favour of the bank), and Facility 4 is an exercise of the bank's statutory right of Set-off (adjusting a debit balance in one account against a credit balance in another account of the same person)
options.B: Facility 3 is a Pledge and Facility 4 is a Mortgage
options.C: Facility 3 is a Lien and Facility 4 is a Hypothecation
options.D: Facility 3 and Facility 4 are both examples of Equitable Mortgage

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Facility 3 is an Assignment (transfer of an actionable claim - the life insurance policy - in favour of the bank), and Facility 4 is an exercise of the bank's statutory right of Set-off (adjusting a debit balance in one account against a credit balance in another account of the same person)

Assignment represents a transfer of an existing or future debt, right or property (such as a life insurance policy, an actionable claim) in favour of the bank, giving the assignee an absolute right over the moneys assigned - matching Facility 3. Set-off is the statutory right of a creditor to adjust, wholly or partly, a debit balance in the debtor's account against a credit balance lying in another account of the same debtor, in the same name and capacity - matching Facility 4.

case_facts_html: CA Priyal Deshmukh is the Statutory Central Auditor of Northgate Nationalised Bank for the financial year 2025-26. During the course of the audit, her engagement team identifies a series of unusual round-tripping entries at one branch that appear designed to camouflage a large corporate account from slipping into the NPA category, along with weaknesses in the branch's internal control and inspection system relating to credit sanctioning. CA Deshmukh must now finalise (i) her main audit report to be submitted to the Central Government, (ii) the Long Form Audit Report for the bank, and (iii) any additional communication required with the regulator regarding the suspicious entries she has found.
question_html: What must CA Deshmukh's main audit report to the Central Government state, as required for a nationalised bank?

options.B: Whether the financial statements present a true and fair view, whether transactions coming to her notice were within the bank's powers, whether returns from offices/branches were adequate for her audit, and any other matter she considers should be brought to the Central Government's notice
options.A: Only the total number of employees in the bank as on the balance sheet date
options.C: Only whether the bank's branches are adequately air-conditioned
options.D: Only the market price of the bank's shares as on the balance sheet date, if listed

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) Whether the financial statements present a true and fair view, whether transactions coming to her notice were within the bank's powers, whether returns from offices/branches were adequate for her audit, and any other matter she considers should be brought to the Central Government's notice

In the case of a nationalised bank, the auditor's report to the Central Government must state whether the financial statements present a true and fair view, whether transactions coming to her notice were within the bank's powers, whether returns from offices and branches were adequate for the audit, and any other matter she considers should be brought to the Central Government's notice - which would include the round-tripping entries discovered.

case_facts_html: CA Priyal Deshmukh is the Statutory Central Auditor of Northgate Nationalised Bank for the financial year 2025-26. case_facts_html: CA Ojas Barve, while auditing the Profit and Loss Account of Riverstone Urban Bank for the year ended 31st March 2026, notices the following: (i) A term loan to Kavya Ceramics Ltd. was classified as NPA for the first time during the current year; interest of ₹6 lakh accrued and credited to the income account in the previous year on this loan remains unrealised. (ii) A bill purchased from Meherzad Exports, discounted at the close of the year, carries discount income of ₹2 lakh, of which ₹80,000 relates to the period falling after the year-end. (iii) The bank renegotiated the repayment schedule of a corporate loan to Windrose Logistics Ltd. during the year, earning a renegotiation fee of ₹3 lakh, covering a rescheduled credit extension period of three years from the date of renegotiation.
question_html: How should the ₹6 lakh interest income relating to Kavya Ceramics Ltd.'s term loan, accrued and credited in the previous year but remaining unrealised, be treated in the current year?

options.A: Since the advance has become NPA for the first time in the current year, the entire ₹6 lakh interest accrued and credited to income in the past period should be reversed or provided for, as it has not been realised
options.B: No reversal is needed since the income was correctly recognised on accrual basis in the year it was earned
options.C: Only 50% of the ₹6 lakh needs to be reversed, with the balance carried forward indefinitely
options.D: The interest should be reversed only if the loan is also reclassified as a Loss Asset

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Since the advance has become NPA for the first time in the current year, the entire ₹6 lakh interest accrued and credited to income in the past period should be reversed or provided for, as it has not been realised

When an advance becomes NPA as at the close of a year, the entire interest accrued and credited to the income account in past periods should be reversed or provided for if not realised. Since Kavya Ceramics' loan has become NPA in the current year and the ₹6 lakh interest recognised last year remains unrealised, it must be reversed/provided for in the current year.

case_facts_html: Meritserve Engineering Ltd. has availed a working capital facility of ₹500 crore under a consortium arrangement led by Zenbank Ltd. (the Lead Bank), with four other member banks. CA Rukmini Salaskar is the statutory branch auditor of one of the member banks, Coralcrest Bank Ltd., which holds a 15% share of the consortium limit. During the audit, CA Salaskar notes that: (i) remittances from Meritserve Engineering Ltd. during the last quarter of the year were pooled entirely with Zenbank Ltd., and Coralcrest Bank Ltd. did not receive its proportionate share of these remittances; and (ii) Zenbank Ltd., in its capacity as Lead Bank, computed the overall Drawing Power for the borrower for the month of March 2026 based on the latest stock statement and communicated the allocated share to each member bank, including Coralcrest Bank Ltd.
question_html: On what basis should CA Salaskar assess the classification of Coralcrest Bank Ltd.'s share of the Meritserve Engineering advance?

options.D: On the basis of the record of recovery in Coralcrest Bank Ltd.'s own books; since remittances were pooled with the Lead Bank and Coralcrest did not receive its share, the account should be treated as not serviced, and therefore an NPA, in Coralcrest's books
options.A: Automatically as Standard, since the consortium as a whole is being serviced through the Lead Bank
options.B: On the basis of the classification adopted by Zenbank Ltd. alone, without independent assessment by Coralcrest Bank
options.C: As NPA only if all five member banks simultaneously agree on the classification

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) On the basis of the record of recovery in Coralcrest Bank Ltd.'s own books; since remittances were pooled with the Lead Bank and Coralcrest did not receive its share, the account should be treated as not serviced, and therefore an NPA, in Coralcrest's books

Consortium advances should be classified based on the record of recovery of the respective individual member banks. Where remittances are pooled with one bank and the bank receiving them does not part with the share of other member banks, the account should be treated as not serviced (and hence NPA) in the books of the other member banks - here, Coralcrest Bank Ltd.
